title: That $20,000 Cash-Out Is Actually a $213,000 Decision
description:
Cashing out an old 401(k) early feels like free money. After a 10% penalty and taxes, $20,000 becomes $13,600 in your pocket today. Left alone until retirement, that same $20,000 could grow into something very different. We run the real numbers.

This video uses AI-generated narration and visuals.

#Shorts #401k #retirement #personalfinance

segments.text: Twenty thousand dollars sitting in an old four oh one k. Cashing it out early feels like free money, right now.
It isn't free. A ten percent early withdrawal penalty, plus it's taxed as ordinary income - call it twenty two percent federal. That's thirty two percent gone before you see a dollar.
Twenty thousand dollars on paper. Thirteen thousand six hundred dollars in your account.
Now compare that to just... leaving it. Thirty five years until sixty five, growing at a seven percent average return, no other contributions.
Same twenty thousand dollars. One version hands you thirteen thousand six hundred today. The other hands your future self two hundred thirteen thousand five hundred thirty two dollars.
The penalty isn't really ten percent. It's every year of growth between now and the day you would have needed it.
